title.narrative: Life-saving humanitarian assistance to address the most critical needs of internally displaced people, living in informal settlements in Hudet Woreda

description.narrative: ltpgtOWDA, in partnership with RESDO (sub-partner), is proposing a multi-sectoral life-saving project to provide critical assistance to the vulnerable conflict-displaced people in Hudet Woreda, Daawa Zone, Somali Region. ltbrgtHudet Woreda, bordering Oromia region, and has been hotspot for inter-communal conflict between Somalis and Oromo. It hosts large number of both protracted IDPs and new arrivals displaced in the latest round of violence which erupted in July 2025. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project's objectives are to:ltbrgt1. Provide critical life-saving assistance to vulnerable conflict-displaced people in informal settlements. ltbrgt2. Build the resilience of the affected communities to withstand future shocks.ltbrgt3. Increase institutional capacity of the Woreda administration to provide sustained assistance to the affected people. ltbrgt ltbrgtThe project period will be nine months and will address the most critical humanitarian needs of the vulnerable displaced communities through integrated responses tailored to the specific needs and capacities of the target communities, that also builds their resilience. For efficiency, the project will precisely target the recently displaced households. However, the host communities will benefit from some of the project supported services like rehabilitated water schemes and health facility-based services. The project will strictly adhere to the “do-no-harm” principles and actively promote social cohesion between IDPs and the host communities to prevent any tension.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project focuses on six sectors: WASH, ES/NFI, Health, Nutrition, General protection and GBV, and MPCA. Activities under each sector are carefully designed to address the immediate needs of the IDPs and also build their resilience. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe total proposed budget for this project is 899,999.99 USD allocated as follows: ltbrgt16% for WASHltbrgt29% for ES/NFIltbrgt20% for Healthltbrgt18% for nutritionltbrgt09% for MPCAltbrgt08% for general Protection and GBV. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRESDO, the sub – IP, will manage the ES/NFI sector and will be responsible for 29% of the total budget. This partnership with RESDO is important. It will contribute to the localization efforts by increasing the operational continuity and development of RESDO. OWDA will support RESDO by providing trainings on project management, financial management, M and E, and security and risk management. That will strengthen RESDO's capacity. Moreover, RESDO’s prior experience in implementing emergency shelter projects in Tuliguled Woreda, Fafan zone, will add value to this partnership and facilitate smooth implementation of the project. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will support 51,635 individuals, including 45,315 IDPs. Out of that IDPs 9,027 are women, 15,346 are girls, 8124 are men, and 12,638 are boys. For the host community, total of 6,500 will be reached. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey activities for each sectorlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtWASH activitieslt/bgt: Rehabilitation one strategic borehole construction one institutional and two blocks communal latrines provision of WASH NFI items for 620 HHs and organizing four rounds of hygiene and sanitation campaigns. ltbrgtltbgtES/NFI activitieslt/bgt: Distribution complete emergency ES/NFI to 1,711 vulnerable HH, ltbrgtltbgtHealth activitieslt/bgt: Provision of primary healthcare through MHNT training of Public Health Emergency Management training on Infection prevention and control establishing and training rapid response teams responding to outbreaks, organizing MISP and rehabilitation of two damaged Health facilities. ltbrgtltbgtNutritionlt/bgtltbgt activities:lt/bgtltspangt Supporting routine screening treating SAM and MAM cases, provision of food for care takers lt/spangtstrengtheningltspangt reporting systems lt/spangtltspangtand transportation of Nutrition supplies to facilities. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtMPCA activitieslt/bgt: Distribution of MPC to 200 HHs to cover their basic needs for three months facilitating linkage for the target HHs to other assistance and services. ltbrgtltbgtGeneral protection and GBV activitieslt/bgt: Cash intervention sensitization and awareness campaign GBV case management dignity kit distribution referral service for survivors and establish and train CFRM committee. ltbrgtlt/pgt
